reasons: [reasoning_validity/major] D1 [verdict (sentence 4); CL2; C1 assessment] The verdict says 'none of the tier-0 surfaces going to production has been independently tested'. The sources do not support that. The web SAML/OIDC login flows and the admin console were in scope of the Brightwater test (E1), and both are tier-0 surfaces. That test is old and may not reflect the current code, but the honest statement is that the tested surfaces are 32 months stale and may have changed (the changelog is only an excerpt), while SCIM, the session service, the device grant and passkeys were never tested. The same overreach shows up in CL2 ('the code going to production on these surfaces') and in the C1 line 'Every major surface changed since then was untested'. These read as if the changelog were complete and the login and admin code were known to be unchanged or known to be changed. Neither is established.

[alternatives_counterarguments/major] D2 [counterarguments; tradeoffs[0], tradeoffs[1]; alternatives] The strongest case for approval is never addressed: the risk of the status quo. The draft does not ask what the organisation uses today for 2,300 employees (no SSO, a legacy IdP, manual provisioning or slow deprovisioning). It does not weigh whether delay keeps a weaker posture in place, such as password sprawl or orphaned accounts after terminations. 'Deferral protects all 2,300 accounts' (tradeoffs) assumes the current state is safer, without evidence. The staging tradeoff also assumes there is an existing IdP ('two IdP paths') without checking.

[alternatives_counterarguments/major] D3 [alternatives; practicalImplications] Obvious decision options are missing. (a) Approve SSO separately from SCIM, for example SSO only, with JIT or existing-tool provisioning until provisioner-v2 is tested. This follows directly from the draft's own finding that SCIM is the least-assured surface; at present it only appears as a parenthetical ('SCIM limited to a non-critical app'). (b) A customer-commissioned independent test of its own Keystone tenant (SCIM, device grant, session invalidation, OTP rate limiting) during a pilot. This would not depend on the vendor's cooperation, which the draft treats as the main bottleneck. (c) Evaluating alternative IdP vendors if Keystone cannot provide assurance.

[coverage/major] D4 [verdict (pilot conditions); alternatives 'Staged or limited rollout'; practicalImplications[3]] The decision objective explicitly asks for conditions with 'named compensating controls, contractual or evidence deliverables, deadlines'. The draft names the controls and deliverables but gives no deadlines for any vendor deliverable apart from 'before Friday' for the written request. It also sets no pilot parameters: no population size or cap, no duration, no exit or expansion criteria, and no trigger for rolling back if deliverables slip. The draft itself flags the risk that a 'pilot quietly becomes permanent', but it never defines the guardrail that would prevent it.
D2 and D5 have remedy 'both' (status-quo risk evidence; current NIST 800-63B-4 rate-limit text); D1/D3/D4 reanalysis

[decision_usefulness/major] D1 [verdict (pilot guardrails, last sentences); alternatives 'Staged or limited rollout (pilot) with guardrails'; practicalImplications[4]; CL17] The pilot guardrails added in draft 2 do not cover the outcome most likely to matter: confirmation that the known Highs are still open. Rollback fires only on 'any new open High or Critical finding', and a freeze happens only on a 'missed deadline'. Suppose the 30-day retest or closure evidence (guardrail e) arrives on time and shows BW-04 (session survives password reset) or BW-07 (admin export IDOR) is still open, or that BW-11 has no rate limiting. Then neither trigger fires, because the findings are not new and the deadline was met. The pilot would keep running with confirmed account-takeover persistence and a directory-exposure flaw. The draft's own unlock criteria require closure of BW-04, BW-07 and BW-11, so the guardrails should match: rollback or suspension when delivered evidence confirms any of them is still open, not only when a new finding appears. Excluding admins from the pilot does not neutralise BW-07, because the draft itself (edgeCases[1]) says a lower-privilege session may be able to exploit it.
D1 major decision_usefulness (pilot triggers miss confirmed-open known Highs), remedy reanalysis
